what: Rather than scrolling the document, the wheel·finger pushes a single value p — 700px of wheel is p 1, and each push overwrites one .9s power2.out tween toward p so it settles with a long tail when the hand stops (finger 1.6×). ↓·PageDown / ↑·PageUp cross between set sections with power3.inOut (distance × .9s, .9~2.4s). Uses --fx-p on the board and each layer’s own range progress --fx-k, and fires an fx:clock event — a one-screen story where 3D·text·cards all change on the same clock

options.step: Wheel px per 1 of p, default 700
options.glide: Glide time after the wheel (s), default .9 · 0 for immediate
options.stops: Sections to cross by key (comma separated), e.g. 0,1,3.3,4.3

use: <main data-fx="wheel-clock" data-fx-wheel-clock="max: 6; stops: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6" style="height:100vh"><section data-fx-part="layer" data-from="1" data-to="2" style="opacity: var(--fx-k)">…</section></main> · Move it with a button: el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('fx:go', { detail: { p: 3 } }))

from.where: shared.js clock — original scroll.js (pxPerStep 700 · glide .9 power2.out · touch 1.6 · keys move between sections with power3.inOut, length = distance × .9 into a range of .9~2.4)

note: A wheel rolled over [data-own-wheel] inside a panel is not intercepted by the panel (own scrolling like maps and lists). Touch is listened to as passive and not blocked, so write the panel to cover the whole screen so the document doesn’t scroll separately
